newsitem.title: UK: UK High Court rules against BT over Oftel powers.
newsitem.headline: UK High Court rules against BT over Oftel powers.

text.p: The British High Court on Friday ruled against British Telecom in a legal challenge over new powers for the Oftel watchdog body.
Oftel has introduced a Fair Trading Condition into BT's licence which seeks to prohibit any abuse by a dominant operator or the making of any restrictive anti-competitive agreements.

BT had accepted the condition and retail price controls set out by Oftel in August but said its acceptance of Oftel's increased powers was subject to confirmation of their lawfulness by judicial review.

"The condition can, as intended, be extended to all other communications companies operating in the UK, starting with Mercury and those receiving an international facilities licence," BT said. It will take effect on December 31.
BT said the right approach to introducing tighter controls on anti-competitive behaviour was through legislation and urged the government to give the matter urgent consideration.
Oftel Director General Don Cruickshank welcomed the ruling.

"With the granting yesterday of 44 international licences - ending the international facilities duopoly - the UK is now the most open telecommunications market in the world," Cruickshank said in a statement.

"Today's confirmation of the lawfulness of the Fair Trading Condition, which appears in those International Facilities Licences as well as BT's licence, means that the UK regulatory regime will be well equipped to deal with the dynamic competitive market of the future," he added.
